items.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025
items.q: Fred Hersch is one that has really taken the place of the Mike Renzis of the world.

ctx.x: Absolutely. In fact one of the things that they don’t teach anywhere is how to be an accompanist to a pianist, as a pianist, how to accompany a singer. Because that’s an art in itself. And a lot of the young guys are not learning that at all and they’re all over the place. It was a story from NYU but they gave me somebody that my singer said, “I could sing that at my lesson but I can’t sing —” I said no wonder, I couldn’t come in on that intro in a million years because it was just all over the place and he’s…

now come on, you’re supposed to make that singer — lift her up, make it wonderful. And there are very few young — Fred Hersch is one that has really taken the place of the Mike Renzis of the world. But there are not many guys around that really accompany well and they certainly don’t teach it in the schools.

At the end of this article I have from you, you used the word “joy” a lot. And you just made me think of it because a good accompanist has to be joyful in what they do. That has to bring them joy that they are assisting a musical performance.
